name: Hepatic Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Radiologic demonstration of abnormal direct arterial to venous communication within the liver on Doppler ultrasound, CT angiography, or MRI
Presence of clinical signs such as hepatic bruit or high-output cardiac failure attributable to hepatic shunting
Exclusion of other causes of hepatic vascular abnormalities such as cirrhosis or portal hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging evidence of hepatic AVM plus at least one major clinical sign
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiologic supported by clinical findings; biopsy is rarely needed.

pathognomonic.notes: Audible bruit over the liver due to turbulent blood flow
Resulting from significant arteriovenous shunting in the liver
searchTerms: heart failure with high blood flow

common.notes: Enlarged liver due to vascular malformation
Due to hepatic congestion or ischemia

occasional.notes: Due to liver dysfunction or biliary compression
From portal hypertension or heart failure

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic liver disease
searchTerms: fatigue related to chronic liver problems

occasional.notes: Due to altered hepatic blood flow

rare.notes: Due to variceal rupture from portal hypertension
Compression of bile ducts by vascular malformation

laboratory: Elevated bilirubin in cases with biliary obstruction
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing direct arteriovenous communications
CT angiography or MRI demonstrating hepatic vascular malformations and shunting
Angiography confirming abnormal hepatic arterial to venous connections
genetic: May be associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) gene mutations (ENG, ACVRL1) in some cases
other: Signs of high-output cardiac failure on cardiovascular examination

distinguishingFeatures: Benign vascular tumor with different imaging characteristics
Usually asymptomatic and no high-output cardiac failure
Often related to trauma or iatrogenic causes
May present with localized symptoms rather than diffuse malformation

redFlags: Sudden onset of high-output cardiac failure
Rapidly worsening abdominal distension or pain
Signs of hepatic encephalopathy or severe liver dysfunction
references: Shovlin CL. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: pathophysiology, diagnosis and treatment. Blood Rev. 2010 Mar;24(6):203-19.
Lee EW, et al. Hepatic arteriovenous malformations: diagnosis and treatment. Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol. 2010 Nov;33(6):1139-50.
